The metals safety check gives a clear stop when it fails
Depends on a helper whose behavior is not visible here

terms.meaning: a date known only to the quarter of the year, such as Q1
a value showing the project finished early, such as minus 2 months
a check that stops the program if a condition is false

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and usage notes
sections.what: Explains the purpose of the script, notes that the metals group is audited too but has no delay values, and shows the preview and execute modes. Imports the helper functions.
sections.why: Gives the owner the purpose and safe default before running.
sections.watch_out: The header says existing values are never recalculated, so keep that rule if editing.

sections.name: entries
sections.title: Four lithium plant records
sections.what: Lists four lithium mining records, each with a stored delay value and a note on how its dates were read. Two entries describe the same P1000 expansion under different names.
sections.why: Each note explains why the stored value is kept and flagged approximate.
sections.watch_out: A negative delay value means the project finished early, so do not flip its sign when editing.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Guarded run for the lithium audit
sections.what: Checks that the mining-metals group has no delay values, then passes the lithium list to the helper. Any error is printed and the script exits with a failure code.
sections.why: Stops the run before any change if the metals group has delay values, so that group is not marked by accident.
sections.watch_out: If the metals check fails, none of the lithium entries are processed.

summary: Marks four lithium mining projects as having approximate delay values, after first confirming that the mining-metals group has no delay values.
purpose: Record that four lithium mining schedule values rest on quarter-level or fuzzy dates, without changing the stored numbers.
why: The header says existing values are guarded and never recalculated; the metals check is a safety check that the group is untouched.
how: First the script asserts that the mining-metals group has no delay values. If that check passes, it passes four hand-written lithium entries to the shared helper markApproximateDelays under an audit name. Without the execute flag it only reports; with it, the helper writes. The helper's exact rules are not visible here.
inputs: Four hard-coded lithium project IDs, names, stored delay values and notes, plus the database.
outputs: Approximate-delay marks in the database when run with the execute flag. Otherwise a preview. The metals check either passes silently or stops the run.
risks: Two entries describe the same P1000 expansion, one listed under the Pilgangoora name, so a change to one may need a matching change to the other. The entries are hand-typed.
debug: If the run stops at the first step, a mining-metals project has a delay value; find it in the database. If a lithium entry fails, check its ID and stored delay.
